# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate
**Date:** November 7, 2026
**Re:** Braport Seed Genetics, Inc. / Traidir Seed Production, LLC: review of the supply documents before the 2027 Production Season

---

## 1. Bottom Line

I reviewed four documents:

* the Supply Agreement dated October 1, 2026 (Delaware law; five-year Initial Term);
* Statement of Work No. 1 for the 2027 season;
* the Service Level Schedule; and
* the November 4, 2026 production planning meeting notes.

I found **four material issues** that leave Braport exposed. Three of them are made worse by one structural feature, the **order of precedence in Supply Agreement Section 2.3**. Under that clause, if the documents conflict, they govern in this order:

1. the **Service Level Schedule**;
2. then the **Supply Agreement**;
3. then each **Statement of Work**.

This means:

* the Schedule overrides the Supply Agreement wherever they are inconsistent; and
* the SOW, which ranks last, cannot narrow or correct anything in the Supply Agreement or the Schedule.

**Summary of issues**

| # | Issue | Location | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Exclusivity and non-production covenant reaches every crop across the US and Canada | Supply Agreement §4.1, read with §1.1 ("Contract Seed," "Territory") | High |
| 2 | Traidir may assign without Braport's consent, including to a competitor | Supply Agreement §18.2 | High |
| 3 | Germplasm-loss liability pulled back under the 12-month fee cap | Service Level Schedule §6.2 (prevails under SA §2.3) | High (most serious) |
| 4 | Seed-quality, performance and service-credit disputes moved to Iowa law and Polk County courts | Service Level Schedule §8.1 (prevails under SA §2.3) | Medium–High |

**Recommended fix for the precedence clause (applies to Issues 1, 3 and 4).** Amend Section 2.3 so the Supply Agreement controls. The Schedule would prevail only on technical Specifications and Service Level metrics. Proposed language:

> "2.3 **Order of Precedence.** If there is any conflict or inconsistency among the documents forming this Agreement, the documents will govern in the following order: (a) this Supply Agreement; (b) the Service Level Schedule, solely as to Specifications, testing protocols, Service Levels and Service Credits; and (c) each Statement of Work. No provision of the Service Level Schedule or any Statement of Work will limit, expand or modify Articles 4, 9, 12, 18 or 19 of this Agreement unless it expressly refers to the Section being modified and states that it is intended to amend it, and is signed by an officer of each Party."

---

## 2. Issues

### Issue 1: Exclusivity covers every crop and all of North America

**Where it appears**
* Supply Agreement **Section 4.1** (Exclusive Supply).
* Read with the **Section 1.1** definitions of "Contract Seed" and "Territory."
* The agreed scope is in **SOW Section 1.1**.

**What it says**
* Section 4.1 requires Braport to purchase "all of its requirements of Contract Seed in the Territory exclusively from Supplier." It also bars Braport from producing Contract Seed "in the Territory itself or through any other grower."
* Section 1.1 defines "Contract Seed" as "**any seed of any crop produced from Braport Germplasm**."
* "Braport Germplasm" is itself defined broadly: all genetic material Braport owns, licenses or controls, including breeding populations and derivatives.
* Section 1.1 defines "Territory" as "**the United States and Canada**."
* By contrast, SOW Section 1.1 records the deal as hybrid corn seed from Braport parent lines, **grown in Iowa and Illinois**. The meeting notes (item 3.1) confirm both sides understand the program that way.

**Why it matters for Braport**
* Read literally, Braport must use Traidir for **every crop** produced from any Braport germplasm. That would include any soybean, sorghum, wheat or other lines. The restriction covers the whole US and Canada.
* It runs for the five-year Initial Term and every renewal.
* It also bars **Braport's own in-house production** and **any other contract grower**. Braport could not:
  * run its own foundation or seed-increase plots;
  * use a backup grower if Traidir under-delivers; or
  * place production with a grower closer to non-Iowa/Illinois markets.
* The forecasts in Section 4.3 are non-binding, but they do not soften the exclusivity covenant.
* **The SOW does not cure this.** The SOW's narrower scope cannot control because the SOW ranks last under Section 2.3. The overbreadth sits in the Supply Agreement itself, and the Supply Agreement prevails over the SOW. Traidir could therefore treat any non-Traidir production of any Braport-derived seed anywhere in the US or Canada as a breach. That would support damages and a termination claim under Section 16.1.

**Recommended fix**
* Narrow the definitions to the actual deal.
* Carve out in-house and backup production.
* Consider adding a capacity-failure release.

Proposed language:

> "**Contract Seed**" means hybrid corn seed produced from Parent Seed under a Statement of Work.
>
> "**Territory**" means the States of Iowa and Illinois.
>
> "4.1 **Exclusive Supply.** During the Initial Term and any Renewal Term, Customer shall not engage any third-party contract grower to produce Contract Seed in the Territory for commercial sale, other than as permitted by Section 4.4. Nothing in this Agreement restricts Customer or its Affiliates from (a) producing any seed, including Contract Seed, itself or through its Affiliates; (b) producing any seed of any crop other than hybrid corn; (c) producing any seed outside the Territory; or (d) conducting research, breeding, foundation seed, parent seed increase, trial or pre-commercial production anywhere."
>
> "4.4 **Release.** If Supplier notifies Customer under SOW Section 3.4 or otherwise that it expects to deliver less than 90% of the Units allocated to any hybrid, or if Supplier fails a Service Level for Volume (Schedule §4.2), Customer may procure the shortfall from any other grower without breach of Section 4.1."

**Open questions for the client**
* Does Braport have, or plan, germplasm or production programs in crops other than corn, such as soybean, sorghum or wheat?
* Does it produce anywhere outside Iowa and Illinois, including Canada?
* Does it currently use in-house production or any other contract grower? If so, Braport may **already be in technical breach** since October 1, 2026. That affects how hard we push and how we frame the request to Traidir.
* Was a broad exclusivity commercially traded for pricing or capacity? If so, Braport may need to give something back to narrow it.

---

### Issue 2: Traidir can assign freely, including to a competitor

**Where it appears**
* Supply Agreement **Section 18.2**, contrasted with Section 18.1.

**What it says**
* Section 18.1 bars Braport from assigning without Traidir's prior written consent.
* Section 18.2 lets Traidir assign the Agreement or any SOW, in whole or in part, "**without the consent of Customer**," on only 30 days' notice. This expressly includes assignment by merger, consolidation, change of control or sale of all or part of its seed production assets.
* Nothing excludes assignment to a competing seed company.

**Why it matters for Braport**
* Traidir will hold Braport's most valuable asset, its proprietary parent seed (BF-217, BF-231, BF-244, BM-063, BM-071). It will also hold field locations, hybrid identities, volumes and production protocols.
* An assignee could gain custody of that germplasm and the full production relationship. Braport would have no consent right and no termination right. The assignee could be:
  * a competing seed company; or
  * a grower that also produces for a competitor.
* Braport would also stay **locked into exclusivity** (Issue 1) with whoever acquires Traidir.
* "In whole or in part" lets Traidir split the contract. For example, it could keep the Iowa fields and transfer the Illinois fields or the Ames conditioning facility to another entity. This would fragment chain of custody.
* The Article 9 and Article 15 protections would bind an assignee in theory. In practice, the protection a germplasm owner needs is control over *who* holds the material. The asymmetry with Section 18.1 is not commercially justified.

**Recommended fix**
Replace Section 18.2:

> "18.2 **By Supplier.** Supplier shall not assign, delegate or otherwise transfer this Agreement or any Statement of Work, in whole or in part, whether voluntarily, by operation of law, by merger, consolidation or change of control, or by sale of all or any part of its seed production or Conditioning assets, without Customer's prior written consent. Customer may withhold consent in its sole discretion for any proposed assignment to, or change of control in favor of, a Competitor. "**Competitor**" means any person (or Affiliate of a person) that develops, licenses or sells commercial seed or parent-line germplasm, or that produces seed under contract for any such person."
>
> "18.4 **Change of Control.** Supplier shall notify Customer at least 60 days before any change of control of Supplier. On any change of control of Supplier, Customer may terminate this Agreement and any Statement of Work, without liability, by written notice given within 90 days after receiving notice of the change of control. Section 16.4 applies to any such termination."

Fallback if Traidir resists full consent:
* permit assignment to a non-Competitor Affiliate only, on notice; and
* keep the Competitor bar and the Braport termination right on change of control.

**Open questions for the client**
* Is Braport aware of any pending sale, recapitalization or ownership change at Traidir?
* Who are Traidir's other seed-company customers?
* Which companies should appear on a named-competitor list, if Braport prefers a list to a definition?

---

### Issue 3: Germplasm-loss liability is pulled back under the fee cap (most serious)

**Where it appears**
* Service Level Schedule **Section 6.2**.
* It interacts with Supply Agreement **Sections 2.3, 12.2, 12.3(a), Article 9 and Section 9.5**.

**What it says**
* **Supply Agreement Section 12.2** caps each party's total liability at "**the fees paid by Customer in the 12 months preceding the claim**."
* **Section 12.3(a)** carves out of both the cap and the indirect-damages exclusion "Supplier's breach of Article 9, including any loss, diversion or unauthorized propagation of Parent Seed or other Braport Germplasm."
* That carve-out is the uncapped protection Braport bargained for.
* **Schedule Section 6.2** then provides: "**Notwithstanding Section 12.3 of the Agreement**, Supplier's liability for any Germplasm Loss Event, including any related Performance Failure, is subject to the limit in Section 12.2 of the Agreement."
* "Germplasm Loss Event" (SA §9.5) covers any loss, theft, diversion, unauthorized propagation or unauthorized transfer of Braport Germplasm in Traidir's or its subcontractors' possession or control.
* **The Schedule prevails under Section 2.3**, so Schedule §6.2 overrides Section 12.3(a).

**Why it matters for Braport**
* The core risk in this relationship is diversion or unauthorized propagation of parent lines. The value of those lines, including years of breeding investment and future hybrid revenue, likely far exceeds a year of production fees.
* For scale, 2027 fees at the SOW rates come to roughly $6.4 million at full volume. Fees "paid … in the 12 months preceding the claim" could be much lower, for example:
  * early in the term; or
  * before 2027 invoices are paid (payment is 45 days from invoice, and invoicing occurs only on acceptance of each Lot).
* An early-2027 diversion claim could be capped at **near zero**.
* "Including any related Performance Failure" and the broad wording ("any Germplasm Loss Event") may also cap claims under Article 9 more generally. Most Article 9 breaches will involve a Germplasm Loss Event.
* Schedule §6.2 refers to Section 12.2 and does not expressly displace the Section 12.1 consequential-damages exclusion. Traidir could still argue that lost profits from misappropriated lines are excluded. The real-world remedy would then be gutted.
* What survives:
  * injunctive relief under SA §9.6;
  * the $25,000 late-notification service credit; and
  * the 12.3(d) carve-out for gross negligence, fraud or willful misconduct. Traidir could argue that 6.2's "notwithstanding Section 12.3" overrides even that carve-out for Germplasm Loss Events.
* None of these is a substitute for full damages for negligent loss or employee or subcontractor theft.

**Recommended fix**
Preferred approach: delete Schedule Section 6.2 in its entirety. Also amend SA Section 2.3 as proposed in Part 1. If Traidir insists on keeping a provision, replace §6.2 with a confirmatory clause:

> "6.2 **Germplasm Loss Events.** For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Schedule limits Supplier's liability for any Germplasm Loss Event or any breach of Article 9 of the Agreement. Sections 12.1 and 12.2 of the Agreement do not apply to that liability, as provided in Section 12.3(a) of the Agreement. Service Credits under Section 5 for Germplasm Notification or Chain-of-Custody Records are in addition to, and do not reduce, that liability."

Consider also adding:
* a dedicated germplasm-value insurance requirement; and/or
* liquidated damages per pound of diverted Parent Seed set at a meaningful level. Liquidated damages should come only as a floor, not a cap.

The current Section 14.1(b) insurance covers only replacement value of the physical seed. It does not cover the value of the genetics.

**Open questions for the client**
* What is Braport's internal valuation of the five parent lines (development cost, expected hybrid revenue)? We need this to show Traidir why a fee cap is inadequate and to size any fallback.
* Was Schedule §6.2 raised or negotiated by Braport's business team? Or did it come in with Traidir's quality and operations draft without legal review?

---

### Issue 4: Seed-quality disputes moved to Iowa law and Polk County courts

**Where it appears**
* Service Level Schedule **Section 8.1**.
* It conflicts with Supply Agreement **Sections 19.1 and 19.2**, read with Section 2.3.

**What it says**
* SA Section 19.1 chooses the **laws of the State of Delaware**.
* SA Section 19.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to the **state or federal courts located in Wilmington, Delaware**.
* Schedule Section 8.1 provides that the Schedule, and "any dispute concerning Performance Failures, Service Credits or Seed Quality," is governed by the **laws of the State of Iowa**. It requires such disputes to be resolved exclusively in the state or federal courts in **Polk County, Iowa**.
* Because the **Schedule prevails under Section 2.3**, the Iowa clause controls for those disputes. Delaware law and the Wilmington forum do not govern them.

**Why it matters for Braport**
* The disputes moved to Iowa are the core commercial disputes in a seed production deal:
  * germination and genetic purity failures;
  * rejected Lots;
  * volume shortfalls; and
  * service credits.
* "Seed Quality" is defined broadly in Schedule §1.1. "Performance Failure" includes Germplasm Notification and Chain-of-Custody Service Levels (Schedule §§4.5–4.6). This means **germplasm-related disputes could also be pulled to Iowa**.
* One dispute would likely be split. For example, a contaminated Lot raises:
  * Seed Quality (Iowa);
  * warranty under SA §11.2 and indemnity under Article 13 (Delaware); and
  * possibly Article 9 issues.
* That invites:
  * parallel proceedings;
  * threshold fights over which clause a claim falls under;
  * inconsistent results; and
  * extra cost.
* Traidir is an Iowa LLC with its facility in Ames. The clause gives Traidir a home forum and Iowa seed-law and UCC treatment on the disputes most likely to arise.
* The Section 19.4 jury waiver and Section 19.3 escalation step may not clearly apply to Iowa proceedings under the Schedule.

**Recommended fix**
Delete Schedule §8.1, or replace it with:

> "8.1 **Law and Forum.** This Schedule, and any dispute concerning Performance Failures, Service Credits or Seed Quality, is governed by Section 19.1 of the Agreement and is subject to Sections 19.2, 19.3 and 19.4 of the Agreement. Nothing in this Schedule affects the application of mandatory seed labeling or certification laws of the state where Contract Seed is produced or sold."

Also amend SA Section 2.3 as proposed in Part 1, so Article 19 cannot be displaced by a Schedule.

**Open questions for the client**
* Does Braport have any business reason to accept an Iowa forum for operational disputes? For example, cost of litigating near the fields or facility.
* If so, a fallback is to keep Delaware law and forum and allow expedited expert determination of testing disputes. This would build on the third-laboratory retest mechanism in Schedule §3.4.

---

## 3. Other Observations

* **Liability cap mechanics (SA §12.2).** The cap is the fees paid by Braport in the 12 months preceding the claim. It is mutual and also protects Braport. Because the cap measures fees *paid* rather than fees *payable*, it is low early in the term and between seasons. Even apart from Issue 3, consider:
  * a floor (for example, the greater of fees paid in 12 months or a fixed dollar amount); or
  * a measure tied to fees payable under the current SOW.
* **Subcontracting and growers (SA §5.5).** Section 5.5 bars Traidir from subcontracting any growing without Braport's prior written consent. The meeting notes (item 4.1) say Traidir "has secured grower commitments on all planned fields." *Open question:* are these third-party growers? If so, Braport should give written consent only after reviewing the grower agreements. Those agreements should flow down the Article 9 and Article 15 obligations. Otherwise Parent Seed will be on third-party farms with no direct contractual protection.
* **Meeting notes.** These are internal working notes and are expressly "not a contract document." They record that no changes to the documents were proposed or agreed. They do not alter any of the issues above.
  * They usefully confirm the parties' shared understanding of the hybrid corn / Iowa-and-Illinois scope, which helps when asking Traidir to narrow Issue 1.
  * That understanding does **not** override the Supply Agreement definitions.

---

## 4. Incomplete or Missing Items in the Folder

1. **Execution status.** All three contract documents show blank signature blocks. The notes state the Supply Agreement "became effective on October 1, 2026." *Please confirm with the client* whether executed versions exist and whether they match these drafts. If the Agreement is already signed, the fixes above must be made by written amendment under SA §20.3. Our leverage is then mainly the 2027 SOW and the upcoming season.
2. **Customer production protocols.** These are referenced in SA §5.2 but not in the folder.
3. **Seed treatment designation.** This is due February 1, 2027 (SOW §5.2). The notes say Braport has not yet decided whether to supply the materials itself or have Traidir purchase them at cost.
4. **Field legal descriptions and GPS boundaries.** These are due February 15, 2027 (SOW §4.1).
5. **Approved Parent Seed storage access list.** This is required under Schedule §7.1.
6. **Grower or subcontractor agreements and any §5.5 consents.** See Part 3.
7. **Certificates of insurance.** These are available on request under SA §14.1. We should request them before Parent Seed is delivered on March 15, 2027.
8. **Negotiation history.** There is no redline or correspondence showing how Schedule §§6.2 and 8.1 entered the documents. This would help in framing the conversation with Traidir.

---

## 5. Suggested Next Steps

1. **Confirm the open questions with the client**, in particular:
   * execution status;
   * other crops, geographies and growers;
   * the value of the parent lines; and
   * any Traidir ownership changes.
2. **Raise Issues 3 and 1 first with Traidir.** Both should be resolved before Parent Seed is delivered by March 15, 2027.
3. **Package the fixes as a single amendment.** It would revise:
   * SA §§1.1, 2.3, 4.1, 18.2 and new 18.4; and
   * Schedule §§6.2 and 8.1.

   The amendment should be signed under §20.3.

I am happy to prepare a draft amendment and a short client briefing note once we have the client's answers.

# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate
**Date:** November 7, 2026
**Re:** Braport Seed Genetics, Inc. / Traidir Seed Production, LLC: Review of Supply Agreement, 2027 SOW, Service Level Schedule and Planning Notes

---

## 1. Summary

I reviewed the four documents in the folder:

- Supply Agreement dated as of October 1, 2026 (the "**SA**")
- Statement of Work No. 1 for the 2027 Production Season (the "**SOW**")
- Service Level Schedule (the "**SLS**")
- Production planning meeting notes of November 4, 2026

**Order of precedence frames this review.** Under SA Section 2.3, conflicts are resolved in this order:

1. the Service Level Schedule first;
2. then the Supply Agreement;
3. then each Statement of Work.

This ranking affects how the problems below play out. The SLS can override protections in the SA. The SOW cannot narrow the SA.

**Three issues need attention before Braport relies on the documents for the 2027 season:**

| # | Issue | Location | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Exclusivity and non-production covenant covers every crop across the US and Canada | SA §4.1, read with §1.1 ("Contract Seed," "Territory") | High |
| 2 | Traidir may assign freely, including to a competitor | SA §18.2 | High |
| 3 | Germplasm-loss liability pulled back under the 12-month fee cap | SLS §6.2, prevailing under SA §2.3 | High |

**The meeting notes do not change the analysis.** They are marked "Internal working notes. Not a contract document." They expressly record that no changes to the SA, SLS or SOW were proposed or agreed. They confirm the commercial understanding: hybrid corn, Iowa and Illinois, 180,000 Units. They do not amend the contract documents. Under SA §20.3, any amendment requires a signed written instrument.

---

## 2. Issues

### Issue 1: Overbroad exclusivity and non-production covenant

**Location:** SA Section 4.1, read with the Section 1.1 definitions of "Contract Seed" and "Territory."

**What the documents say:**

- SA §4.1 requires Braport, during the Initial Term and any Renewal Term, to "purchase all of its requirements of Contract Seed in the Territory exclusively from Supplier." Braport also may not "produce Contract Seed in the Territory itself or through any other grower."
- "Contract Seed" (SA §1.1) means "any seed of any crop produced from Braport Germplasm."
- "Braport Germplasm" is itself broad. It covers all genetic material Braport owns, licenses or controls, including progeny and derivatives.
- "Territory" (SA §1.1) means "the United States and Canada."
- The SOW (§1.1) records the actual arrangement as "hybrid corn seed from Braport parent lines, grown in Iowa and Illinois." The planning notes (§3.1) confirm that understanding.

**Why it matters for Braport:**

- **The covenant reaches far beyond the deal.** Read together, SA §§1.1 and 4.1 lock Braport into Traidir for:
  - every crop developed from Braport Germplasm, which would include any soybean, sorghum, wheat or other lines;
  - every production location in the United States and Canada;
  - for at least five years (SA §3.1), and longer through automatic one-year renewals unless Braport gives notice 180 days before the end of the term (SA §3.2).
- **It bars more than outside purchasing.** Braport could not produce in-house or use any other contract grower anywhere in North America. That includes growers it may already use for other crops or regions.
- **It is one-sided.** Traidir makes no reciprocal volume or exclusivity commitment. SA §4.3 makes Braport's forecasts non-binding. In addition, SA §4.2 commits Traidir only to the capacity needed for volumes in each SOW.
- **Existing contracts may already be in breach.** Any current arrangements Braport has with other growers could put it in breach from the Effective Date (October 1, 2026).
- **The SOW does not cure this.** The flaw sits in the SA's own definitions. Under SA §2.3 the SA outranks the SOW, so the narrower corn, Iowa-and-Illinois scope in SOW §1.1 cannot control. If the SA and SOW conflict, the SA's broad definitions govern. The fix must be made in the SA itself.

**Recommended fix:**

Narrow the definitions and the covenant, and carve out Braport's own and existing production.

> **"Contract Seed"** means hybrid corn seed produced from Braport Germplasm under a Statement of Work.
>
> **"Territory"** means the States of Iowa and Illinois.
>
> **4.1 Exclusive Supply.** During the Initial Term, and subject to Section 4.4, Customer shall obtain from Supplier its requirements of Contract Seed for production in the Territory, to the extent of the volumes set out in the Statements of Work executed by the Parties. Nothing in this Agreement restricts Customer from (a) producing any seed, including Contract Seed, itself or through its Affiliates; (b) producing any seed other than hybrid corn seed, or any seed outside the Territory, through any grower; or (c) engaging any other grower for volumes that Supplier is unable or unwilling to commit to in a Statement of Work, or following any failure by Supplier to meet the Volume Service Level in Section 4.2 of the Service Level Schedule.
>
> **4.4 Existing Arrangements.** Section 4.1 does not apply to Customer's arrangements with the growers listed in Exhibit [__] or to any renewal of them.

**Further options:**

- Limit exclusivity to the Initial Term only, rather than carrying it into Renewal Terms.
- Add a right for Braport to step out of exclusivity if Traidir has a chronic failure under SLS §6.4.

**Open questions for the client:**

- Does Braport currently produce, or plan to produce, any seed from its germplasm with other growers or in-house? This covers other crops and corn outside Iowa and Illinois.
- Are any of those arrangements in place now? If so, we need to assess possible current breach risk and whether a side letter is needed pending amendment.
- Did Braport intend any real exclusivity in favor of Traidir, even within corn in Iowa and Illinois? Or was this a non-exclusive production arrangement?

---

### Issue 2: Unrestricted assignment by Traidir

**Location:** SA Section 18.2 (contrast Section 18.1).

**What the documents say:**

- SA §18.1 bars Braport from assigning without Traidir's prior written consent.
- SA §18.2 allows Traidir to "assign this Agreement or any Statement of Work, in whole or in part, without the consent of Customer, on 30 days' written notice." This expressly includes assignment by merger, consolidation, change of control or sale of all or part of its seed production assets.
- Nothing excludes assignment to a competing seed company.

**Why it matters for Braport:**

- **Traidir has custody of Braport's most valuable asset.** It holds Braport's proprietary Parent Seed and related Confidential Information, including:
  - hybrid identities and pedigrees (the SOW lists female and male parents);
  - field locations;
  - volumes and pricing.
- **A competitor could acquire that custody.** A competing seed company could buy Traidir, or Traidir's Ames assets, and then hold Braport's parent lines and run its production. Braport would have no consent right and no termination right.
- **Partial assignment is also permitted.** Braport's program could be split across entities. Chain of custody and accountability would then be fragmented.
- **The SA's protections do not reach this risk.** The germplasm protections (Article 9) and confidentiality (Article 15) bind an assignee on paper. They do not address the commercial and trade-secret risk of a competitor gaining physical custody and operational knowledge.
- **The existing termination rights do not help.** Braport's termination rights (SA Article 16) are limited to breach, insolvency and germplasm breach. None is triggered by an assignment or change of control.
- **The asymmetry is unjustified.** Braport cannot assign even to an Affiliate or in a sale of its business.

**Recommended fix:**

Replace SA §18.2 and conform §18.1.

> **18.1 By Customer.** Customer may assign this Agreement or any Statement of Work, in whole, without Supplier's consent (a) to an Affiliate, or (b) to a successor to all or substantially all of the business or assets to which this Agreement relates. Otherwise, Customer shall not assign this Agreement without Supplier's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.
>
> **18.2 By Supplier.** Supplier shall not assign, transfer, delegate or subcontract this Agreement or any Statement of Work, in whole or in part, whether voluntarily, by operation of law, merger, consolidation, change of control or sale of assets, without Customer's prior written consent, which Customer may withhold in its sole discretion where the proposed assignee or acquirer is, or is an Affiliate of, a Competitor.
>
> **18.4 Change of Control.** Supplier shall give Customer at least 60 days' prior written notice of any proposed Change of Control of Supplier. On a Change of Control of Supplier, or any transfer of the facilities or Production Fields used to perform this Agreement, Customer may terminate this Agreement and any Statement of Work by written notice, without liability. Section 16.4 will then apply, and Supplier shall immediately return all Parent Seed and Braport Germplasm.
>
> **"Competitor"** means any person that develops, licenses, produces or sells commercial seed or parent-line germplasm of any crop, other than solely as a contract grower for third parties.
>
> **"Change of Control"** means any transaction or series of transactions by which a person or group acquires control (as defined in "Affiliate") of Supplier.

**Open questions for the client:**

- Is Braport aware of any pending sale, investment or affiliation involving Traidir?
- Who are the competitors of greatest concern? This would let us consider a named-party list in addition to the general definition.

---

### Issue 3: Germplasm-loss liability brought back under the fee cap

**Location:** SLS Section 6.2, prevailing under SA Section 2.3, read with SA Sections 12.2 and 12.3(a).

**What the documents say:**

- SA §12.2 caps each Party's total liability at "the fees paid by Customer in the 12 months preceding the claim."
- SA §12.3(a) excludes from the cap, and from the §12.1 exclusion of indirect damages and lost profits, "Supplier's breach of Article 9, including any loss, diversion or unauthorized propagation of Parent Seed or other Braport Germplasm."
- SLS §6.2 then provides: "Notwithstanding Section 12.3 of the Agreement, Supplier's liability for any Germplasm Loss Event, including any related Performance Failure, is subject to the limit in Section 12.2 of the Agreement."
- Under SA §2.3, the SLS prevails over the SA. So SLS §6.2 controls.

**Why it matters for Braport:**

- **The uncapped remedy Braport bargained for is removed.** Read together, SA §§2.3, 12.2, 12.3(a) and SLS §6.2 take away Braport's uncapped remedy for germplasm loss.
- **The cap is small relative to the risk.** For the 2027 season, total fees at full volume are roughly $6.4 million (180,000 Units at $34.50–$36.25 per Unit). The cap could be well below that early in the relationship, because it counts only fees *paid* in the preceding 12 months. Payment terms are 45 days, and SA §6.1 provides that fees arise only on acceptance. A claim arising during the 2027 growing season, before any lots are accepted and paid, could face a cap at or near zero.
- **Germplasm loss is worth far more.** Loss, theft, diversion or unauthorized propagation of proprietary parent lines can destroy value worth many multiples of a year's production fees. Examples include years of breeding investment, competitive advantage and future hybrid revenue.
- **Indirect damages may also be excluded.** Because §6.2 says "notwithstanding Section 12.3," a court could read it as also restoring the §12.1 exclusion of consequential damages and lost profits for germplasm loss. Those are precisely the damages Braport would suffer.
- **"Germplasm Loss Event" is defined broadly.** Under SA §9.5 it covers essentially any Article 9 failure involving loss of control of Braport Germplasm. The override therefore guts SA §12.3(a) almost entirely.
- **Other protections remain but are not enough.** Injunctive relief (SA §9.6), termination (SA §16.3) and the $25,000 late-notification Service Credit remain. The arguable carve-out for gross negligence, fraud or willful misconduct in §12.3(d) is uncertain in light of §6.2's override language. None of these substitutes for full damages.

**Recommended fix (in order of preference):**

**(a) Delete SLS §6.2** and replace it with:

> **6.2 Germplasm Loss Events.** Supplier's liability for any Germplasm Loss Event is governed by Article 12 of the Agreement, including Section 12.3(a), and is not limited by Section 12.1 or Section 12.2 of the Agreement. Service Credits for any Germplasm Loss Event are in addition to, and do not limit, Customer's other rights and remedies.

**(b) Fix the precedence clause** so the SLS cannot override the SA's core risk allocation. Amend SA §2.3:

> **2.3 Order of Precedence.** If there is any conflict or inconsistency among the documents forming this Agreement, the documents will govern in the following order: this Supply Agreement, then the Service Level Schedule, then each Statement of Work; provided that the Service Level Schedule governs as to the Specifications, Service Levels and Service Credits. No provision of the Service Level Schedule or any Statement of Work will modify Articles 9, 12, 13, 15, 18 or 19 of this Agreement unless it expressly refers to the provision being modified and states that the Parties intend to modify it.

Doing both is the safest course. Fix (b) also protects against future SLS amendments having the same effect.

**(c) Fallback, if Traidir will not accept an uncapped exposure:** a separate, substantially higher super-cap for Article 9 breaches. This would be a fixed dollar figure tied to the value of the germplasm, not to fees. It should keep the §12.3(d) carve-out for gross negligence, fraud and willful misconduct uncapped. The insurance requirement in SA §14.1(b) covers Parent Seed only "at full replacement value," which will not reflect its genetic value. It should be paired with a requirement that Traidir carry coverage responsive to germplasm loss, if available.

**Open questions for the client:**

- Was SLS §6.2 negotiated or flagged during the deal, or did it appear in a later Traidir draft?
- How does Braport value the parent lines being delivered (BF-217, BF-231, BF-244, BM-063, BM-071)? We need this to size any fallback super-cap.
- Has the SLS already been signed?

## 3. Other observations (lower priority)

- **SA §2.3 is the root cause of Issue 3.** Ranking an operational schedule above the main agreement is unusual. It means any future SLS amendment by the quality leads could alter core legal terms. Under SLS §8.2, those leads meet annually to propose changes. I recommend amending §2.3 as proposed under Issue 3(b) in any event.
- **Specifications.** SA §1.1 defines "Specifications" by reference to both the SLS and the SOW. The SOW (§6.1) defers to the SLS, so there is no current conflict. Customer's "written production protocols" referred to in SA §5.2 are not in the folder.
- **No volume commitment by either party beyond the SOW.** This is consistent with Braport's interests. However, it underscores that the exclusivity in SA §4.1 gives Traidir protection without a reciprocal guarantee.
